name: High Route (Cascade Crest full traverse)
region: North Cascades (Mount Redoubt to Mount Shuksan area)
best_season: Jul-Aug optimal; spring/fall: variable snow cover and bridge stability
hazards: Crevasse fields across multiple glaciers (Peat, Cascade, Chickamin) — bergschrund crossings critical early season; rope rescue proficiency and probe technique essential; June-August most hazardous with bridge collapse risk

Navigation complexity through remote terrain with frequent whiteout conditions — multiple high passes with confusing routefinding; GPS/map mandatory; incorrect pass selection leads to major rerouting or scramble into worse terrain
Rapid alpine weather shifts with afternoon thunderstorms common Jul-Aug — exposed ridgeline position creates lightning hazard; summit storms typically develop 1-3pm; start alpine sections pre-dawn
Glacial meltwater stream crossings increase dramatically in afternoon — melt intensity varies by time of day; early morning crossing essential; rope belay required for major water hazards
Exposed camp sites on alpine terrain — avalanche exposure from >35° slopes above camp locations; wind cornice formation on ridge camps; lightning exposure during afternoon storms

Sustained multi-day high altitude (8,000+ ft) exertion — altitude sickness risk on repeated climbing days; cumulative fatigue increases navigation and camp-hazard errors; descent time criticality increases with party fatigue
Remote evacuation logistics — 15+ miles from nearest road; helicopter rescue difficult in alpine basin terrain; party must be self-sufficient for crevasse rescue and emergency medical response
Fixed rope and anchoring on steep glacier sections — anchor quality variable on ice and snow; ice-screw placement critical; party size must support rope management and multi-pitch glacier travel
sources: Mountain Project High Route descriptions and trip reports (2024-2026)
RMI guide company alpine traverse resources
seasonal_window: Jul-Aug optimal with minimal snow; Jun-Sep marginal; spring: variable glacier conditions; fall: early storms

name: Enchantments Loop (North Cascades)
best_season: Aug-Sep optimal; Jul: lingering snow on high passes; spring/early summer: unstable glacier conditions
hazards: Colchuck Glacier crevasse field — multiple crevasses with variable snow bridges; mid-season (Jul-Aug) highest risk with bridge collapse; rope mandatory; bergschrund crossing complex; glacier rope rescue knowledge essential

High-altitude navigation through alpine basin with multiple peak options — whiteout conditions common; terrain traps and gullies create navigation hazard; GPS/topo map required; turnaround time critical

Colchuck and Dragontail Peak objective hazards from above — rockfall from warming peaks in afternoon; serac collapse risk from hanging glaciers; stay out of fall lines; early morning exit from peak zone
Extreme altitude exposure on summit ridge — Dragontail Peak summit section has 40+ knot winds typical; one-hand-off belay standard; exposure consequence is fatal; helmet essential
Camp site avalanche exposure — suitable camp locations limited; must avoid slopes >30° above camps; cornice formation on ridge camps; wind loads accumulate overnight

Stream crossings and glacial meltwater hazards — Colchuck Lake outlet and Enchantment Lakes drainage increase melt rate in afternoon; early morning crossing essential; current hazard increases temperature dependent

Exposed scrambling sections with rockfall hazard — Cashmere Col and Pawnee Pass approaches have loose rock; multiple parties create rockfall hazard; compact party and helmet required; stay vigilant for rocks from above
sources: Mountain Project Enchantments Loop trip reports (2024-2026)

seasonal_window: Aug-Sep optimal with stable conditions; Jul: lingering snow on Col/Pass crossings; Jun-Jul: ice tools may be needed

name: Ptarmigan Traverse
area: North Cascades (Mount Shuksan to Mount Baker area)
best_season: Aug-Sep optimal; Jul: lingering winter conditions, ice tools likely needed; Jun and earlier: deep snow, crevasses dangerously hidden
hazards: Crevasse fields on multiple glaciers (Easton, Curtis, Squak glaciers) — most dangerous Jun-Jul with concealed crevasses under thin snow bridges; rope rescue mandatory; hazmat rescue is difficult in remote area
Steep icefall sections — Shuksan Arm ice cliffs and Curtis Glacier headwall create active icefall zones; afternoon warming increases ice/rock fall risk; early morning passage critical

Winter/spring variant avalanche exposure — early season route can have significant avalanche hazard on >35° approaches; wind-loaded aspects particularly risky; NWAC forecast essential; party must assess stability actively

Navigation complexity through interconnected glacier system — whiteout conditions eliminate visual landmarks; multiple pass options exist; wrong glacier selection leads to major rerouting; GPS/compass/map mandatory

Extreme altitude combined with exposed camp sites — sustained high altitude (8,000+ ft) over 3 days; camp locations limited and exposed; weather exposure significant; descent time criticality essential
Ice tool proficiency requirement for summer variant — even in late summer, Curtis Glacier sections can have blue ice or thin ice; microspikes insufficient; ice tools and mixed climbing skill required
Remote rescue logistics — far from help; party must be self-sufficient; evacuation helicopter rescue difficult due to terrain; 6+ person party recommended for crevasse rescue proficiency
sources: Cascade Alpine Guide (Beckey) - Ptarmigan Traverse section
